question:
Consider the following statements.

1. At present, there are no active volcanoes in India.

2. The main cause of volcanic eruption is associated with plate tectonics, orogeny and sea-floor spreading processes.

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Statement 1:** At present, there is one active volcano in India, which is the **Baratang Island Volcano** in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Hence, this statement is **incorrect**. 
• **Statement 2:** Volcanic eruptions are primarily caused by geological processes such as **plate tectonics**, **orogeny** (mountain-building), and **sea-floor spreading**. These processes result in the movement of magma from beneath the Earth's crust to the surface. Hence, this statement is **correct**. 
• The movement of tectonic plates leads to the creation of faults and fractures, enabling magma to rise to the surface through volcanic vents. 
• Volcanic activity is most common along **plate boundaries**, such as the **Ring of Fire** in the Pacific Ocean, where subduction zones and divergent boundaries exist. 
• India is relatively stable geologically, but the Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie close to tectonically active regions, resulting in the presence of an active volcano. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Active Volcano in India:** 
• **Baratang Island Volcano** is India's only active volcano, located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. 
• The Baratang volcano primarily exhibits **mud volcanoes**, which release gases and mud rather than lava. 
• It is situated along the **subduction zone** between the Indian Plate and the Burma Plate, contributing to its activity. 
• **Causes of Volcanic Eruption:** 
• Volcanic eruptions are driven by the accumulation of **magma**, which is molten rock beneath the Earth's surface. 
• Key geological processes involved include: 
• **Plate Tectonics:** Movement of plates leads to magma generation at subduction zones and divergent boundaries. 
• **Orogeny:** Mountain-building processes can create pressure imbalances, leading to magma movement. 
• **Sea-floor Spreading:** Magma rises at mid-ocean ridges where tectonic plates diverge. 
• Other factors like **gas pressure** and **temperature changes** also contribute to eruptions. 
• **Types of Volcanic Activity:** 
• **Active Volcanoes:** Volcanoes that erupt frequently or show continuous activity. Example: Mount Etna in Italy. 
• **Dormant Volcanoes:** Volcanoes that have not erupted in recent history but may become active in the future. Example: Mount Fuji in Japan. 
• **Extinct Volcanoes:** Volcanoes that are unlikely to erupt again. Example: Mount Kilimanjaro in Africa. 
• **Global Volcanic Zones:** 
• The **Pacific Ring of Fire** is the most active volcanic zone, with over 75% of Earth's active volcanoes. 
• Other notable zones include the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge** and East African Rift Valley. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Geological Context of India:** 
• India lies in the **Indo-Australian Plate**, which is relatively stable compared to other tectonic plates. 
• The Himalayan region, however, is geologically active due to the collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate. 
• Seismic activity and minor volcanic features are observed in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands due to proximity to subduction zones. 
• **Historical Volcanic Activity:** 
• India's geological history includes extinct volcanic formations, such as the **Deccan Traps**, formed during massive volcanic eruptions around **66 million years ago**. 
• The Deccan Traps are one of the largest volcanic provinces globally and played a role in the extinction of dinosaurs. </ul
